info.name: DoFi Backend API
info.description:
# DoFi Backend API

Covers JWT authentication (sign in/me/sign out), DoFi officer user management, role management with permission assignment, the permissions catalog, public self-registration for Jetty Managers and Fishermen, officer Profiling (pre-registering a Company Profile a fisherman later matches by IC number), FINS Approval (the Fisherman/Jetty Manager registration review queues), the full Manifest module (Vessel self-service + approval, the port-out/capture-report/port-in lifecycle, Capture Reports and their nested resources), master reference data, and the fish species Dictionary.

## Environments

Select one of these Postman environments before running anything — they provide `base_url` and the seeded admin credentials:

| Environment | base_url | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **DoFi Backend - Local** | `http://localhost:3000` | Local Docker dev stack (`docker compose up`). Safe to use freely. |
| **DoFi Backend - Staging** | `http://46.202.163.155:3012` | Shared staging server, no TLS yet. Shared with other testers — be considerate with writes/deletes. |

## Authentication flow

1. Run **Auth → Sign In**. On success the response includes the JWT both as `data.access_token` in the JSON body and in the `Authorization` response header (`Bearer <token>`) — pick whichever your client finds easier. A test script automatically saves it into the `jwt_token` collection variable.
2. Every other request in this collection uses collection-level Bearer auth (`{{jwt_token}}`) by default — no need to copy/paste tokens manually between requests. The **Manifest** folder is the one exception; see its own section below.
3. Run **Z - Sign Out (run last) → Sign Out** when you're done. This revokes the JWT (devise-jwt JTI denylist) and clears `jwt_token`. Anything run after Sign Out needs a fresh Sign In first.

## Roles & permissions model

Each `User` belongs to one `Role` (e.g. the seeded `DoFi Officer`), and each `Role` has many `Permission`s identified by a `code` (e.g. `roles.create`, `dofi_officer_users.update`). Endpoints are authorized via Pundit policies that check the signed-in user's role permissions:

- **Roles**: `roles.list`/`roles.view`, `roles.create`, `roles.update`, `roles.delete`
- **Users**: `dofi_officer_users.list`/`.view`, `.create`, `.update`, `.delete`
- **Permissions**: read-only catalog, available to any authenticated user

A failing permission check returns `401` (no/invalid session) or `403` (authenticated but not allowed), depending on the failure mode.

## Manifest module: two extra tokens, per-request auth

The **Manifest** folder is the one place in this collection that needs more than one authenticated identity in the same run: officer Profiling/approval steps use the collection default (`{{jwt_token}}`), but vessel/manifest creation and lifecycle submission (`submit_port_out`, `submit_port_in`, ...) must run as the fisherman — `Manifests::Create` derives `company_profile` from `current_user`, so an officer token can't be used for those calls. Requests that need the fisherman's identity override `request.auth` (Bearer, one of `{{manifest_fisherman_jwt_token}}` / `{{manifest_commercial_fisherman_jwt_token}}` / `{{manifest_skip_demo_jwt_token}}`) instead of inheriting the collection default — look for a request-level Authorization tab that differs from its folder/collection parent if you're browsing in the Postman UI. The folder demonstrates both `fisherman_category` guard paths side by side (Small-Scale (Full-Time) skips Jetty/officer approval at port-out/port-in; Commercial requires it, including a full request-amendment → resubmit → approve cycle), plus the Skip Capture Report path and the draft-only delete guard. Like the rest of this collection's demo flows, it uses hardcoded IC numbers/boat numbers — re-running the whole folder a second time against a database that already has a prior run's data will 422 on "IC number has already been taken" partway through (same caveat as **Users → Create User**).

## List endpoints: filter, sort & pagination

`GET` index endpoints (`/api/v1/permissions`, `/api/v1/roles`, `/api/v1/users`) accept Ransack query params for filtering/sorting and Pagy params for pagination:

- **Filter**: `q[<attribute>_<predicate>]=<value>`, e.g. `q[name_cont]=officer`, `q[status_eq]=active`.
- **Sort**: `q[s]=<attribute> <asc|desc>`, or repeat `q[s][]=...` for multiple sort keys.
- **Paginate**: `page` and `limit` query params (roles/users only — the permissions catalog is not paginated).
- Non-whitelisted attributes (e.g. `encrypted_password`) are silently ignored rather than erroring or leaking data through the search index.

Full contract: `docs/api/search-filter-sort-pagination.md` in the backend repo.

## Soft delete

`DELETE /api/v1/users/:id` soft-deletes via the `Discard` gem — the record is excluded from default scopes (so a subsequent `GET` returns `404`) but stays in the database for audit purposes.

## Manifest module: fisherman vs Web Admin paths

Between FINS Approval and Manifest sits a `Vessels` folder: it logs each demo fisherman in via BruneiID and creates/approves their vessel, kept separate from Manifest (per-folder scoping) but unable to live inside Auth or Profiling because it depends on FINS Approval having already approved the fisherman.

Manifest itself is split into `Manifest - Fisherman` and `Manifest - Web Admin`. The Web Admin folder can't just reuse the Fisherman folder's manifests for its Update/amendment-cycle demos (they're no longer in an editable/pending state by the time Web Admin runs), so it creates two small throwaway manifests of its own — the same self-contained-folder pattern as Auth and Vessels.

Manifest List/Show/Update/Tab Counts are split by audience: fisherman-facing endpoints live under `/api/v1/fisherman/manifests` (list/show/create/destroy/tab_counts + the port-out/port-in submit-resubmit-skip lifecycle, scoped to the signed-in fisherman's own company), while officer/jetty-manager-facing endpoints live under `/api/v1/approvals/manifests` (list/show/update/tab_counts + the approve/request-amendment lifecycle, seeing every company). Nested resources (`capture_reports`, `expense`, `fish_capture_details`, `fishing_gear_details`, `minor_fishermen`) stay unprefixed at `/api/v1/manifests/:manifest_id/...` since both audiences reach them (e.g. the officer's `verify`/`request_amendment` on a capture report) and per-record authorization already scopes access correctly regardless of path.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Authenticates with username/password and returns the JWT both as `data.access_token` in the JSON body and in the `Authorization` response header (`Bearer <token>`), plus the signed-in user's payload (including their role and full permission list). This request's test script auto-saves the token to the `jwt_token` collection variable, so every other request in the collection picks it up automatically. Browser JS clients should prefer `data.access_token` over the header unless the server's CORS config exposes `Authorization` (`Access-Control-Expose-Headers`).

Creates a DoFi officer user. Requires `dofi_officer_users.create`. `password`/`password_confirmation` are optional — omit them (as here) and the server auto-generates a password, returned once as `data.temporary_password` (never shown again after this response); `position`/`unit`/`username` are required for this role. See **Create User - With Admin-Supplied Password** below for supplying your own password instead. The response's `data.id` is auto-saved to the `user_id` collection variable for the requests below. Re-running this without changing `username` will 422 on a persistent environment (e.g. staging) since a prior run's user already exists — change the body or clean up the previous test user first.
Submits a DoFi Officer user with no position/unit/username to confirm these are required for this role (422 with details), rather than a `500` or a silently-created invalid record.

Creates a DoFi officer user with an admin-chosen password instead of an auto-generated one. When `password`/`password_confirmation` are supplied, they're used as-is and `data.temporary_password` is omitted from the response (nothing was auto-generated to show). Uses a different `username` from the plain **Create User** request to avoid a uniqueness collision; re-running on a persistent environment (e.g. staging) will 422 unless the username is changed or the previous test user is removed. Does not overwrite the `user_id` collection variable used by the requests below.
Fetches a single user by id, including their role. Requires `dofi_officer_users.view`.

item.name: Profiling
item.description:
Officer-facing CRUD for `CompanyProfile` (the "Add Profiling" screen). `CompanyProfile` is one row per **company** (or, for Small - Scale (Full-Time), one row per **individual** fisherman — see CompanyProfile#individual?, which just makes company-shape fields optional for that registration_type); person-level data (Owner/Admin) lives on separate `CompanyProfileContact` rows (`belongs_to :company_profile`). Officers pre-create a profile — an Owner contact (required) and optionally an Admin contact — before a fisherman of *any* registration_type, including Full-Time, can self-register and match against it by IC number (see Registrations → Fisherman - Company Profile Lookup / Register). Requires `profiling.*` permissions.

The "Owner + Admin"/"Owner Only" examples below deliberately use the same `ic_no` (`01-192839`), `company_name` (`Azri Fish Sdn Bhd`), and `rocbn_no` (`RC20390923`) as the Registrations folder's Commercial Fisherman example, and "Create Profiling (Individual - Small-Scale Full-Time)" uses the same `ic_no` (`01-555555`) as the Registrations folder's Full-Time example, so running this folder first makes those downstream requests resolve against real data instead of 404ing.

request.description: Requires `profiling.view` or `profiling.list`.

item.name: Contacts
item.description:
`CompanyProfileContact` sub-resource — add, edit, or remove a single person on an existing company without touching the company row or any other contact. This is the real fix for "add an Admin to a company profiled last week": before this endpoint existed, the only way to do that was resubmitting Profiling → Create, which duplicated the Owner every time. Requires the same `profiling.*` permissions as the parent resource.

Run after "Create Profiling (Owner Only)" above — these requests add a second person (Admin) to that Owner-only company, then edit and remove just that person.

request.description: Adds an Admin to the Owner-only company created earlier, without resubmitting any company-level fields and without touching the existing Owner contact. Requires `profiling.create`.

exec: pm.test('Contact is linked to the target company_profile', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.company_profile_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('owner_only_company_profile_id')));

request.description: Missing `full_name`, `ic_no`, `gender`, and `ic_colour` — no row is persisted.
Edits just this contact — the company row and any other contacts are untouched.
Removes just this Admin contact — the company profile (and its Owner contact) stay kept. Contrast with "Delete Profiling (soft)" below, which discards the whole company and everyone on it.

Soft-deletes the company **and** all of its kept `CompanyProfileContact` rows together in one transaction (`CompanyProfiles::Destroy`) — deletes the standalone Owner-only profile created above (not the Owner+Admin pair, which Registrations below still needs).

item.name: Registrations
item.description: Public self-registration endpoints for Jetty Managers and Fishermen. No `Authorization` header is required — all four endpoints are unauthenticated. The expected flow before hitting these endpoints is: (1) user scans a BruneiID QR code, (2) BruneiID callback returns `ic_number` + `name` to the FE, (3) FE calls `GET /registrations/status` to check whether an account already exists for that IC, then routes to the appropriate register form or redirect.

request.description:
Registers a new Jetty Manager account (role kind: Jetty Manager). All five fields are required. The account is created with `status: pending` — same as Fisherman registration, an officer must approve before the user can log in.

The `ic_number` and `name` are typically pre-filled from the BruneiID callback; `unit`, `position`, and `contact_no` are entered by the user on the registration form.

A random secure password is generated server-side — the user never sets one. Future authentication is via BruneiID QR re-scan, not email/password.

request.description:
Fisherman-only endpoint (`POST /api/v1/fisherman/manifests`). This demo sends only the required `companies_vessel_id`, but the full accepted `manifest` payload is:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `companies_vessel_id` | uuid, required | Must belong to an **approved** vessel owned by the fisherman's company. |
| `companies_captain_id` | uuid, optional | Must belong to an **approved** captain owned by the same company. |
| `port_out_id` / `port_out_datetime` / `port_out_area` | optional | Port Out Detail — can be filled at creation or later via Update. |
| `port_in_id` / `port_in_datetime` / `port_in_area` | optional | Port In Detail — same as above, usually filled once at sea/returning. |
| `zone_id` / `zone_area` / `longitude` / `latitude` | optional | Fishing zone / location detail. |
| `has_minor_fishermen` | boolean, optional | Flags that minor fishermen will be added via the nested Minor Fishermen endpoints. |
| `crew_ids` | array of uuid, optional | Existing `CompaniesCrew` records to snapshot onto this manifest. |
| `ad_hoc_crew` | array of objects, optional | One-off crew not in the company roster: `crew_name`, `ic_number`, `passport_number`, `position`, `nationality`, `date_of_birth`. |

**Expenses are not part of this payload.** They're set via a separate call once the manifest exists (1:1 with the manifest itself, not tied to a Capture Report) — see "Create Manifest Expense" further down this folder, which posts to `.../manifests/:manifest_id/expense`.

The manifest starts in the `draft` status (`is_draft: true` in the response) and stays editable/deletable until `submit_port_out` is called.

Every field is optional at creation (offline-first: the client may create a bare shell before zone/location is known, then fill it via update or the nested resources below) — `zone_area` here is just for a more realistic example.

Singular nested resource (1:1 with the manifest) — `create` and `update` both upsert (`manifest.manifest_expense || manifest.build_manifest_expense` then update), so the client doesn't need to track whether the row already exists. Returns 200, not 201, since the controller doesn't set an explicit created status for either verb. Expenses belong to the manifest itself (fuel/ice/rations entered once at Port-Out time), not to a Capture Report — they don't depend on one existing.

`companies_fishing_gear_id` is optional (`belongs_to ..., optional: true`) — omitted here for simplicity. Pass a `CompaniesFishingGear` id (from `POST /api/v1/company_profiles/:id/fishing_gears`, an Approvable sub-resource like Vessel) to auto-snapshot its `name`/`gear_type`/`specification` instead.

Offline-queue flush: each row carries a client-generated UUID; re-syncing the same id is idempotent (find-or-create by that id), and a row whose id already belongs to a *different* capture report fails just that row rather than the whole batch. Replace the two placeholder UUIDs above with real client-generated ones in practice.

Requires `manifest_approvals.approve`. Transitions `port_out_status` `pending` → `approved` and `manifest_status` → `at_sea`.
